Description: A basalt victory stele in Aramaic, set up by an Aramean king (most likely Hazael of Damascus) boasting of victory over Israel and Judah. Its fragments were reused in a wall at Tel Dan and reassembled after discovery.
BiblicalSignificance: The stele contains the phrase 'House of David' (bytdwd), the earliest extra-biblical reference to David as founder of Judah's royal line. For readers who anchor hope in God's promise to David, it is a stone witness that David was a real king whose house neighbouring nations knew by name.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the phrase reads ‘House of David’ and dates to the 9th century BC; debate centers on the stele’s author (most often Hazael of Damascus) and which kings’ deaths it boasts of.
RelatedPeople: King David; Hazael, King of Syria; Jehu; Ahaziah
